title: Peter Sinkamba v Judicial Complaints Commission and Attorney General [2024] ZMCC 23 (29 October 2024)
case_name: Peter Sinkamba v Judicial Complaints Commission and Attorney General
issue_tags: order of stay — already-implemented decision principle
Judicial (Code of Conduct) Act No. 13 of 1999
Judicial Complaints Commission jurisdiction (and review of its 11 October 2017 ruling)
Order X rule 2(1) Constitutional Court Rules — interim orders
Order IX rule 20(1) CCR — mode of commencement
Section 4 Constitutional Court Act No. 8 of 2016 — single-judge powers
Vangelatos v Metro Investments Limited — followed
Joshua Ndipyola Banda v Attorney General — followed
Article 2 standing — every person to defend the Constitution
outcome_detail: Summons by the Petitioner (Peter Sinkamba) for an order of stay of implementation of the Judicial Complaints Commission's ruling of 11 October 2017 dismissed (paragraph [42]: "I accordingly dismiss the summons"). Mulife JC (single judge in chambers) held the summons was misconceived and frivolous because the impugned decision had already been implemented at the time the summons was launched, and under settled principle an order of stay cannot issue where the decision sought to be stayed has already been implemented (paragraphs [38]–[41], applying Vangelatos v Metro Investments and Joshua Ndipyola Banda v Attorney General). The Judge declined to consider the question of locus standi because its determination was reserved for the full Court under section 4 of the Constitutional Court Act. Parties bear their respective costs (paragraph [43]).
